details: The United States and Iran have halted military strikes against each other for a third consecutive night, signaling a potential de-escalation as diplomatic talks intensify. US Ambassador to the UN, Mike Waltz, stated that President Trump is giving diplomacy a chance, although military assets remain in the region. This pause follows nearly two weeks of tit-for-tat attacks that had disrupted a previous ceasefire. Oil prices reacted by dropping, reflecting eased supply disruption fears.
title: US and Iran Pause Strikes Amid Diplomatic Efforts

details: US intelligence agencies are investigating whether Russia assisted Iran in recent drone attacks on CIA facilities in the Persian Gulf. The investigation focuses on potential Russian provision of targeting intelligence or advanced drone technology. While no definitive conclusion has been reached, the effectiveness and precision of the strikes, coupled with Russia's cooperation with Tehran, have raised concerns about a covert Russian offensive against US intelligence operations.
title: US Investigates Possible Russian Role in Iranian Strikes on CIA Facilities

details: The Trump administration has imposed new tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on imports from over 80 countries, including the UK, EU, China, and Canada. These new duties, effective July 24, 2026, replace earlier tariffs that were struck down by the US Supreme Court and are justified under claims of inadequate enforcement against forced labor. The move has sparked criticism globally and caused Asian stock markets to decline.
title: Trump Imposes New Tariffs on Over 80 Countries, Global Markets React

details: The European Union has approved its 21st package of sanctions against Russia, which includes targeting 14 cryptocurrency platforms across various jurisdictions. The measures, agreed on July 22-23, 2026, aim to prevent Russia from evading financial restrictions and introduce a new power for a full third-country ban on crypto-asset services used by Russia. This package also imposes asset freezes on 94 banks and expands transaction bans.
title: EU Broadens Sanctions Against Russia, Targeting Crypto Platforms

details: The Trump administration has informed Congress that it will not complete the spending of $400 million in authorized aid for Ukraine until fiscal year 2029. This timeline has drawn criticism from lawmakers, especially as Ukraine faces critical weapons shortages amidst the ongoing conflict with Russia. The delay introduces uncertainty regarding the sustained level of US support for Ukraine.
title: US Delays $400 Million Aid to Ukraine Until 2029

details: China conducted two days of live-fire drills in the Taiwan Strait from July 23-24, 2026, near its Fujian province. These military exercises, which followed critical remarks from Beijing regarding Taiwan's leadership, signify ongoing tensions in the region. The drills took place shortly after talks between the US Secretary of State and the Chinese Foreign Minister.
title: China Conducts Live-Fire Drills in Taiwan Strait

details: Labour Members of Parliament in the UK are advocating for a permanent ban on cryptocurrency donations to political parties. The push, which gained momentum around July 9, 2026, cites concerns over the transparency of such donations and the potential for foreign interference in the UK's democratic processes. This initiative could lead to stricter regulations on crypto's use in political financing.
title: UK Labour MPs Push for Permanent Ban on Crypto Political Donations
